# Native turn model selection oracle

`oracle.json` uses the fixed TS `GatewaySessionModelBundle` and its real `NativeSessionModelSelectionPolicy` with a recording project resolver and empty session store. It was generated on mbp2 with Node v22.22.0 and the pinned PilotDeck checkout. Only the fixture project path was normalized to `<project>`; error names were removed because the native Services port exposes code and message. The original full output and source are in `_tmp/20261108-native-model-oracle-01/run-extended/oracle.json`.

Run `tsx generate.mts <new-empty-output-directory>` with `/Users/da/ws/pdrs-runner/resources/PilotDeck/node_modules/.bin/tsx` and PATH `/Users/da/opt/node-v22.22.0-icu78-darwin-arm64/bin`; normalize only generated projectKey and omit `reads` and error `name` as above. No network/provider calls are made. The recording resolver asserts project validation order; this is not a claim that it is the real project registry.

`registry-oracle.json` is a second capture using the real `createDialogProjectRegistry`, `listRegisteredWebProjects`, and `createRegisteredWebProjectResolver` over two actual registered directories. It adds 17 cases: empty/non-string/null/absent/relative/aliased project keys, another registered project and General, and truthy/falsy overrides. Capture on mbp2: `PILOTDECK_TS_ROOT=/path/to/pinned/PilotDeck tsx registry.mts <new-output-directory>`. Raw evidence is on mbp2 at `/Users/da/ws/pdrs-worker-wt/control-cli-20261108/_tmp/20261108-runtime-boundary-oracles/registry/raw.json`; the local evidence copy is in `/Users/da/ws/pilotdeck-rs/_tmp/20261108-cli-completion/runtime-boundary-oracles/registry/`. Only actual project/home paths are replaced with placeholders; errors and read counts are preserved.

The native gateway's existing single-project admission boundary rejects the other registered project and General with `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` before selecting a model, rather than reading this host's project configuration for them. Those two rows document the TS capability and are covered by explicit native boundary tests, not counted as equal outputs. Relative cwd is checked in a bounded subprocess to avoid changing the test runner's working directory. The remaining 14 rows plus the original 15 are compared directly.
